Pixel pairs are NOT scored offline (original screenshots are session artifacts); computed-equality is the instrument. The committed scorecard.json (harness run) is untouched.

scorecard.method: enriched contract → core/emit-html (wrapped library tokens + minted token custom properties) vs the ORIGINAL npm package rendering, same pinned Chromium, per combo × interaction; computed-equality over the styled channel set (exact string, no tolerance) + pixelmatch at threshold 0 (AA counted) and 0.1 (AA excluded) — both quoted, never widened

unscored.note: sizeMismatch: our render is a different SIZE than the original, so pixelmatch cannot run — counted in `pairs` (it is a failed pair) and never `perfect`, but NOT averaged: there is no measurement to average. noOriginal: no original screenshot exists, so there was never a pair — excluded from `pairs` entirely.

namedLosses: promotion: non-painting-part: autocomplete-clearindicator <button> renders NO INK in any combo it appears in (visibility: hidden) and no descendant paints — NOT promoted. A part that paints nowhere must carry the fact that hides it (declared display:none / an opacity token) or be refused by name; neither `visibility` nor `content-visibility` has a carried spelling, so promoting this box would put a VISIBLE frame on the canvas that the browser draws nowhere (the general form of the SVG <title> defect)

promotion: orphan-asset-dropped: icon asset "autocomplete-autocomplete-clearindicator" was reconstructed from the svg subtree of part "autocomplete-clearindicator", which this promotion then REFUSED (see the named refusal above) — the asset belongs to no part of the promoted contract and is not carried. Before this door it was committed to the library's assets/icons/ directory and referenced by nothing (measured: examples/mui/assets/icons/autocomplete-autocomplete-clearindicator.svg).
